sections.text: Fix but thy mind on Me, and by My grace thou shalt overcome the obstacles in thy path. But if, misled by pride, thou wilt not listen, then indeed thou shalt be lost.
If thou in thy vanity thinkest of avoiding this fight, thy will shall not be fulfilled, for Nature herself will compel thee.
O Arjuna! Thy duty binds thee. From thine own nature has it arisen, and that which in thy delusion thou desire not to do, that very thing thou shalt do. Thou art helpless.

Okay, we had been discussing chapter 18, Moksha Sannyasi, yoga, Yoga of Liberation through Renunciation. And we are literally coming to the end of Bhagavans advice in this chapter. So in the beginning, obviously, we have seen that the goal of life is to achieve permanent happiness. And we have heard from our scriptures that the only way one can achieve that perfect happiness is either one becomes a sannyasi or a yogi. Everyone else is in the rut of life. And therefore, if thats your goal, to achieve that permanent happiness, you have to either become a sannyasi or a yogi.
So the chapter opened with the definition of sannyasi and yogi. The one who has renounced the sense of I am the doer -- the sense of agency -- is the sannyasi. And who is the yogi? The one who has given up the desire for the fruits of actions is a yogi. So to achieve that permanent happiness, I have to either become a sannyasi or a yogi. And then the prescription came.
It is easier for us to give up the fruits of actions than giving up the sense of agency. Ego is so entrenched in my personality right now that for me to think Im not doing it is more difficult. I must at least give up the expectations for desired results of my actions. I can start with that. If I have to do that, I first have to understand what is action and how it is done, what is my involvement in performing my actions. So we have this detailed analysis of what is action, what is an actor, and what propels that action.
The knowledge propels my actions. My knowledge about myself and this world, my relationship with this world drives me to act in this world. So we have detailed analysis of these three, the action, the actor, and the knowledge. We have seen that all of these three are driven by the texture of my mind. My mind has either a sattvic, Rajasic or tamasic tendencies that will make me either a sattvic actor, Rajasic actor, tamasic actor, that will drive me to the sattvic actions, rajasic actions or tamasic actions. So the texture of my mind is the basis for my life.
Who I am today is a reflection of my mind. With self-introspection, I may come to a conclusion about the makeup of my mind. Right now Im 20% Sattvic, 60% Rajasic, and 20% Tamasic. I really dont have a choice to change that overnight. Just because I go to a doctor to get my blood work done which I do every four months and they say your cholesterol is too high, triglycerides are way out of control.
Just knowing that, I will not be able to change it right away. Neither is there any magic bullet where I can change it overnight. But I can start on a course of action -- a course of action which my doctors constantly, every four months, remind me of. I remember the first month, but for three months I take it easy. And as soon as the fourth month comes, Im vigilant again. I have to be in that prescribed method consistently.
So the first thing is I have to accept my condition. I have to accept that I have the high cholesterol and high triglycerides and I have this propensity to get a heart attack and all that. If I deny that, if Im in denial -- for a long time I denied my blood pressure. I go to my one doctor, my blood pressure always comes out right. I go anywhere else, my blood pressure is very high. So I go to the insurance company, they check and say, Your blood pressure is high.
I said, No, no, you are wrong. Let me go back to my doctor, Ill check it out. For some reason it worked -- every time I go there, my blood pressure is normal. I go anywhere else, my blood pressure is not normal. So I was in complete denial that I have high blood pressure.
Finally I had to accept that I probably do have high blood pressure. So the first step is acceptance -- accepting that I may have this condition. The conditioning which I see as myself is not in my control. It was in my control at one point of time, but it has now become the past. So I have now become who I am because of all my past experiences and actions. And I accept that now I have to work on it.
So first thing I have to do is what comes naturally to me at this time and then take it from there what my goal would be. So Bhagavan said, now if your goal is to achieve permanent happiness, you have come to this conclusion: this is the makeup of your mind. The advice is Sahajam Karma Kaunteya Sadosham Api Na Tyajet. Do the actions which come naturally to you, even though they are imperfect. My chosen field of action may not be the most popular, the most appreciated.
But thats what my nature is. I like carpentry and I want to be a carpenter. I like arts and I want to be an artist. They always have this hungry artists exhibitions because artists go hungry. But thats the chosen field comes naturally to me. The Bhagavan said, sahajam karma kaunteya sadosha bin natya jat.
You cannot give up the field of actions which come naturally to you. First advice, Clear guidance. Stay in the field which comes naturally to you and then go from there. So the next advice is then. Okay, Now I have figured out what my natural field of action is. But how should I act so that Ill get the benefit of that?
The next thing is Asaktah Jitatma -- without attachment and without any expectation. We have seen there are only two paths: either to become a sannyasi or a yogi. Yogi is the one who gives up Karma Phala, the desire for fruits of action. So Ive found the field of my actions.
Im ready to now launch my career in that field or my endeavors -- but without any expectation. I will do what I like to the best I can. What comes out of my actions is not in my control, because I am not the Karma Faladatta. Karma Faladatta is always the Lord, Ishvara, somebody other than me.
I need to leave it to them their duties to perform diligently. I will perform my duty diligently. The Bhagavan said, perform your actions without attachment expectations in the field which comes naturally to you. Doing so, you will develop devotion for me. You will align your thoughts with the one who empowers you to do these actions. So therefore he said, become one with me.
Offer everything to me. And the last few verses which you have seen. He says, bhaktiya mam abhijanati yavat na aschasmi tatvatah tatomam tattvato gnatva visatei tad anantharam. Just by acting in this manner of offering everything to him. As we have seen in detail the previous verses, once I decided the field of my actions, I decided that I am not really the one who empowers me to act. The consciousness functioning through me as my life empowers me to act.
Ill be only able to conduct Gita classes as long as Im alive. The day I drop dead, Gita classes will be history. Thats because my consciousness in me allows me to understand Bhagavad Gita. So the empowering authority is something other than me. That which connects the electricity in this room is the empowering authority for the electricity. We have lights, we have air conditioning.
Right now we are pretty happy. Things are working fine. But when they first rented the place, the electricity wasnt there. He thought, I am the Almighty for this place. Calls me up and says, Not working.
I said, I think the machine is not working. Electricity is not connecting through Dominion Virginia Power. Dominion Virginia Power is the final authority that the electricity comes here. I have a limited power to turn the switch on and off when I need that. But in that limited power, I start thinking because it is always there. I think I am in control and I can turn this thing on and off.
It is only when the power goes out I realize I am just a Nimitta Matra. Virginia Power decides whether I have electricity or not. As long as that electricity is functioning through this space, I can control this space. When Dominion Virginia Power connection is disconnected, no matter how many times I turn the switch on and off, nothing happens. Bhagavan said, you need to recognize this fact that you are connected to me as the supreme consciousness which is functioning through you. If you keep that in mind all the time, they will make sure that that connection never gets disconnected.
See, when I design buildings, most buildings have normal electricity connection. And then when there is power outage, the connection goes out. But I designed the emergency shelter. Actually medical examiners office in downtown. Well, you cant have the power go out during emergency. That is the time when theres a disaster.
Thats the time that office becomes most active. They may have all these disaster victims coming to this place. Those pathologists have to work overnight to deal with them. So you need to have a dual power system for that. We connected that building from two different grids. So even though one grid is out, the other grid is connected.
They will never be out of that electrical connection. Thats where you will have this permanent connection. Bhagavan said, if you want eternal happiness, you need to make sure that your connection to me is always connected. And for that, you have to offer everything that you do to me. Remembering constantly that I can only do this because hes functioning through me. With that attitude, you will develop devotion for him.
You will be constantly attached to him. So we both have to have that dual connection. Bhagavan has to have connection with me and I have to have connection with him. That connection when developed, we call it devotion. Its one that devotion takes place. Bhakti mam Avijanati Yavatna Asha asmi Tattvatahara Tatotam tattvoto Gnatva visate tat Anantaram.
By devotion he knows me in essence. Once I become identified completely with someone or something, I know that thing or being in its essence or his essence. He forthwith enters into me the supreme. Once I completely identify myself with the supreme self, I enters into him. In other words, I become one with that supreme being. Sarvakarmani API sada Kurvanaha mat vyapaasrayah mat prasadat avapnothi Saswatam padam avyayam.
The process took place. I gave up identification with my ego. I chose the field of my actions. I started working in the field of my actions without any expectations and offered all my actions to him. Now with that connection I have identified completely with him. So now my life is doing all actions always taking refuge in him with his grace.
Now I have not become happy with my efforts. I have become peaceful and happy with his grace. This space is properly conditioned and lit up right now -- by the grace of Dominion Virginia Power. When their grace is taken away from me, the lights will go away and the air conditioning will go away. As long as I recognize that the lights and air conditioning are not because of me -- not because Im paying the bills, but because of their grace in connecting electricity to this space -- then I will be fine.
Then Ill develop that devotion to Dominion Virginia Power. As soon as the bill comes, pay the bill. Bhagavan said, one who becomes one with me, with this root of actions he has become one with me and therefore he achieves that Saswatam Padam avyayam.

These verses present both the promise and the warning. Verse 58: mat-chitta - with mind fixed on Me, you will overcome all obstacles by My grace. But aham-karat na shroshyasi - if through ego you will not listen, you will perish. The choice is stark: surrender and be carried across all difficulties, or cling to ego and be destroyed. Verse 59 addresses Arjunas specific situation: if through ego you think I will not fight, your resolution is vain - Prakriti will compel you. This applies universally: we cannot escape our nature through willful avoidance.
Verse 60 drives the point home: svabhava-jena nibaddha - bound by your own karma born of your nature, what you do not wish to do through delusion, you will do helplessly. This is not fatalism but psychological truth. Our vasanas (tendencies) are powerful forces that will express themselves. The question is not whether to act but whether to act consciously or be driven unconsciously. Arjuna cannot avoid being a warrior; his nature will assert itself. Better to fight consciously with understanding than to fight unconsciously driven by repressed instincts.
Examine where ego-resistance is preventing you from doing what needs to be done. What are you avoiding through willful stubbornness that your nature will eventually force you to face? The teaching suggests that surrender is not weakness but wisdom - recognizing that fighting against our fundamental nature is futile. Today, identify one area where you are resisting something that aligns with your dharma. Ask: Is my resistance protecting something valuable, or is it merely ego avoiding what feels threatening? Often what we resist most persistently is exactly what we need to embrace.
